agree.reason: The numbers are sound, but Marisol had to chase the last report for four months, and this draft says nothing about that. It also leaves out the unfunded $4,500 a year for running the van, so she has no good reason to recommend yes over her own doubts.

honest.reason: The draft correctly drops the 'double' claim. Still, 'we expect about 9,000 additional pounds' reads firmer than an offer nobody can promise will come again, and 'grown a short drive' away is a small detail the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the right figures from the brief: 3,000 extra pounds a month in harvest season (6,000 to 9,000, about a 50% rise) and about 12% for the year, and it puts the harvest-month rise first, which is the strongest true framing.

right_comparison.reason: It gives the real alternative, which is to keep refusing farm offers it can't move cold, but it doesn't spell out what that costs in pounds each year if nothing changes.

qualification.reason: 'We will report those figures' has no reporting frequency, no named person responsible and no due date, even though quarterly reports and Dave Lin with a 30-day final report were both available. The expected result has no stated check, such as the farm letters.

objections.reason: It mentions the 2023 shelving grant but avoids the late report, gives no explanation or fix for it, ignores the $4,500 a year for insurance and fuel when reserves would drop to $11,000, and doesn't use the two farm letters.

fit.reason: It is a narrative section with clear headings and comes in under the 500-word limit.
